results.heading: Via the cache
results.text:
Via the cache
When you optimistically update your state before performing a mutation, there is a chance that the mutation will fail. In most of these failure cases, you can just trigger a refetch for your optimistic queries to revert them to their true server state. In some circumstances though, refetching may not work correctly and the mutation error could represent some type of server issue that won't make it possible to refetch. In this event, you can instead choose to roll back your update. To do this, `useMutation`'s `onMutate` handler option allows you to return a value that will later be passed to both `onError` and `onSettled` handlers as the last argument. In most cases, it is most useful to pass a rollback function.

At its core, TanStack Query manages query caching for you based on query keys. Query keys have to be an Array at the top level, and can be as simple as an Array with a single string, or as complex as an array of many strings and nested objects. As long as the query key is serializable using `JSON.stringify`, and **unique to the query's data**, you can use it!
